title: Zynodoa chef wins 'Guy's Grocery Games' redemption episode - NewsBreak
text:
By Monique Calello ,
19 hours ago Revenge was officially on the menu in last week's episode of the Food Network's " Guy's Grocery Games ."
Zynodoa chef Laura Fonner won best dish in a special redemption-themed episode after returning to compete against chefs who had previously fallen short of victory.
"Today's trip to Flavortown was brought to you by revenge," Fonner said at the start of the competition, making it clear she wasn't leaving empty-handed.
Her winning dish, sesame ginger-crusted yellowfin tuna with a chili-crunch sushi rice ball, red pepper-raspberry sambal, avocado aioli and raspberry kimchee, will be featured on the Staunton restaurant's menu through Aug. 30.
"This episode is the ninth one I have done with the show, but probably the one I am most proud of only because of the actual theme itself," said Fonner. "If you had known me when I started competing in 2019, then you probably wouldn't believe that I would eventually call out a celebrity chef on national TV.
More: Chef Laura Fonner brings 'fresh air' to Zynodoa kitchen
"When I was younger, I was timid and shy and hadn't necessarily found my voice yet, so to be able to see the progression of my professional and personal life played out on TV has been really amazing."
Fonner first appeared on "Guy's Grocery Games," hosted by celebrity chef Guy Fieri, in 2019 after a producer reached out about a charity-focused episode. At the time, she was leading an initiative that collected surplus food from local restaurants and transformed it into weekly meals for residents staying at a homeless shelter.
Her dumplings won the episode's championship, allowing her to donate half her winnings to the cause.
More: Stand-up comedian coming to Staunton for Friday night show at Visulite
"This show is one of the only cooking shows that genuinely wants to represent you in the best way possible," said Fonner. "They want to see you be the best version of yourself. I have spent many years intentionally surrounding myself with those kind of people, so every time I end up on their set to compete, it feels like home and feels very natural, even when we all know it's a very unnatural situation."
Over the years, Fonner has made nine appearances on the high-energy culinary competition, showcasing technical precision, creativity under pressure and an ability to transform surprise ingredients into restaurant-quality dishes.
"The wonderful support from my patrons is always why I still do what I do," she said. "Not just competition cooking, but the fact that I continue in this career."
Fonner joined Zynodoa last December and called it her dream job during an April interview with The News Leader . The downtown Staunton restaurant has long been a pioneer of the Shenandoah Valley's farm-to-table movement.
Before arriving at Zynodoa, she built a reputation in Virginia's culinary scene while leading the kitchen at Duner's restaurant in Charlottesville, where she became known for thoughtful sourcing, bold flavors and artistic presentation.
Much like her personality, her food emphasizes vibrant flavors, bright colors and plenty of texture.
"I like to layer textures and flavors together," she said. "And I design plates where you don't have to think about how you're supposed to eat it. I love the small dots and the fine details of high-end fine dining, but sometimes even as a chef, I get lost in how I'm supposed to eat it, and it's my responsibility as a chef to plate it in a way where it just eats how it's supposed to."
As for her growing celebrity status from television appearances?
"I have taken quite a few selfies with strangers recently," Fonner said with a laugh.

Monique Calello writes about business, dining and entertainment at The News Leader in Staunton. Reach her at mcalello@newsleader.com .
